messages.subject: Improving my function to input a data frame instead of an array
parts:
Hello folks,

I've written a function that does not scale well with size of the inputs. My experience with java puts me in the mindset of putting everything into a for loop, and I'm sure that's the reason it is very slow. Here's my function, it takes some points and "constructs" a piece-wise function, and then returns the Payout Percent for a given Attainment.

PayoutFunction <- function(Attainments, Breakpoints){
    Slope <- numeric(nrow(Breakpoints))
    Yintercept <- numeric(nrow(Breakpoints))
    for(i in 2:nrow(Breakpoints)){
        Slope[i-1] <- (Breakpoints[i,2]-Breakpoints[i-1,2])/(Breakpoints[i,1]-Breakpoints[i-1,1])
        Yintercept[i-1] <- Breakpoints[i,2] - Slope[i-1]*Breakpoints[i,1]
    }
    Slope[nrow(Breakpoints)] <- Slope[nrow(Breakpoints)-1]
    Yintercept[nrow(Breakpoints)] <- Yintercept[nrow(Breakpoints)-1]
    PayoutPercent <- Attainments
    Breakpoints <- rbind(Breakpoints, c(Inf, NA))
    for(i in 1:length(Attainments)){
        for(j in 1:length(Slope)){
            if(Attainments[i] >= Breakpoints[j,1] & Attainments[i] <= Breakpoints[j+1,1]){
                PayoutPercent[i] <- Slope[j]*Attainments[i] + Yintercept[j]
                break
            }
        }
    }
    return(PayoutPercent)
}

dput(Breakpoints)
structure(c(0, 0.8, 1, 1.1, 1.25, 1.6, 0, 0, 1, 1.6, 3.4, 4.1
), .Dim = c(6L, 2L), .Dimnames = list(NULL, c("Attainment", "Payout"
)))
Attainments <- rnorm(10000000, mean = 1, sd = .09)

Right now this function takes an array Attainments which is a random distribution of numbers. Ultimately I would like my function to calculate the payout for all cells. So if I have a data frame or matrix, I would like to return the same size data frame with the payouts percents. I know I can just add another for loop in my function to loop across the whole data frame, but I'm wondering if there is another way to do it. Any ideas? Thanks

messages.subject: Re: Improving my function to input a data frame instead of an array
parts:
In order to apply a function to a vector or list, type `?lapply` in to your R prompt and read up on that family of functions. The `plyr` and `dplyr` packages expand upon what is available in base R in case `lapply` or its family of functions is not what you are looking for. 

However, my sense is that you could do most of this via vectorized code as functions themselves can be vectorized, e.g., `exp`, there is no need to use `vapply` to apply `exp` to each value, the function is already vectorized.
> exp(1:3)
[1]  2.718282  7.389056 20.085537
> vapply(1:3, exp, numeric(1))
[1]  2.718282  7.389056 20.085537

My suggestion is that, just like you would in Java or any other language, break your problem down in to the smallest parts and write (vectorized as much as possible) functions for each step. 

p.s. Please make sure you reply to the entire group in your responses.
